reason: The hypothesis makes specific mechanistic claims about interface coherency, back-stresses, and dislocation behavior, but cites no prior evidence whatsoever to support these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the specific behavior of coherent vs. incoherent interfaces in high-entropy alloy multilayers under creep conditions.
premises: Coherent interfaces generate localized back-stresses that impede dislocation motion
Incoherent interfaces lack defined stress fields and facilitate dislocation motion
Interface coherency can be controlled by lattice parameter mismatch via minor Al addition
Back-stresses from coherent interfaces retard both dislocation glide and climb
Creep resistance is primarily determined by interface coherency rather than other factors
